insights.title: Bank credit hits ₹223.9L Cr — fresh record, up ₹3.1L Cr
insights.body: Total bank credit outstanding reached ₹223.9L Cr in August 2026, the highest level on record. Volume climbed ₹3.1L Cr period-on-period (₹220.8L Cr → ₹223.9L Cr), continuing the climb from ₹178.7L Cr in January 2025.
insights.implication: August's ₹3.1L Cr addition is larger than July's ₹1.5L Cr gain, keeping bank credit at a fresh all-time high of ₹223.9L Cr in this 36-period record.

inferences: Bank credit outstanding hit ₹223.9L Cr in August 2026, up ₹3.1L Cr from July's ₹220.8L Cr.
The book has grown steadily since Sep 2023, when it stood at ₹151.5L Cr — an addition of roughly ₹72.4L Cr over this 36-period window.
The level sits at or near the maximum of this window, with no pause in the expansion.

insights.title: Bank credit growth stepped up 5.1 points to 16.1% in FY26
insights.body: Bank credit grew 11.0% in the year ending March 2025 and 16.1% in the year ending March 2026. Full-year growth stepped up 11.0% → 16.1%, a 5.1 point acceleration.
insights.implication: The jump from 11.0% in FY25 to 16.1% in FY26 is a 5.1-point step-up between full years, marking a clear shift in the pace of annual bank credit growth.

inferences: Bank credit grew 11.0% in FY25 and 16.1% in FY26, a 5.1-point step-up.
This is an annual measure set only at the March year-end, not a month-to-month trend — it compares the full year ending March 2026 against the one ending March 2025.
The status reads strengthening, with FY26's full-year rate 5.1 points above FY25's.

insights.title: Banks added ₹29.6L Cr net new credit in FY26
insights.body: Banks deployed ₹29.6L Cr of net new bank credit in the year ending March 2026. The figure is locked at ₹29.6L Cr across the window, reflecting the FY26 year-end tally fixed since March 2026.
insights.implication: ₹29.6L Cr is the high point of annual credit additions in this 36-period record, underscoring the scale of FY26's full-year deployment.

inferences: Net new bank credit in FY26 totalled ₹29.6L Cr.
This value holds constant across all 36 periods in the series because it is set once, at the March year-end, and does not update month to month.
It sits at or near the maximum of this window, the largest annual addition in the dataset.

insights.title: Bank credit growth eases to 19.1% YoY from July's 19.3% peak
insights.body: Bank credit grew 19.1% year-on-year in August 2026, just below July's 19.3%. Growth eased 0.25 points (19.3% → 19.1%), pausing the run-up from 16.0% in April to 19.3% in July.
insights.implication: After rising from 16.0% in April to 19.3% in July, growth eased slightly to 19.1% in August — still the second-highest reading in this 24-period window, not a break in the broader climb.

inferences: Bank credit grew 19.1% YoY in August 2026, down from 19.3% in July.
The reading stays well above the p75 mark of 15.7% for this 24-period window, keeping growth in the upper band.
The slight pullback follows a run-up from 16.0% in April through 19.3% in July.

insights.title: Food credit falls to ₹1.12L Cr — third straight monthly drop
insights.body: Food credit outstanding stood at ₹1.12L Cr in August 2026, down from ₹1.18L Cr in July. Volume fell ₹0.06L Cr period-on-period (₹1.18L Cr → ₹1.12L Cr), the third consecutive monthly decline since May's ₹1.37L Cr peak.
insights.implication: Food credit has declined for three straight months after peaking at ₹1.37L Cr in May, yet at ₹1.12L Cr it still sits in the upper range of this window — the pullback hasn't erased most of the earlier run-up.

inferences: Food credit outstanding fell to ₹1.12L Cr in August 2026, down ₹0.06L Cr from July's ₹1.18L Cr.
This is the third straight monthly fall since the ₹1.37L Cr peak in May 2026 (June ₹1.32L Cr, July ₹1.18L Cr, August ₹1.12L Cr).
Even after three months of decline, the level stays above the upper range (p75) of this 36-period window.

insights.title: Food credit YoY growth jumps to 145.8% — highest in this window
insights.body: Food credit grew 145.8% year-on-year in August 2026, the highest rate in this 24-period window. Growth accelerated 37.9 points (107.9% → 145.8%), extending the run-up from 94.1% in May and 105.1% in June.
insights.implication: The 37.9-point jump to 145.8% is the sharpest single-period acceleration in this food-credit series, taking growth past every prior reading in this 24-period window.

inferences: Food credit grew 145.8% YoY in August 2026, up 37.9 points from July's 107.9%.
This extends a run-up from 94.1% in May and 105.1% in June to 107.9% in July — four straight months of acceleration.
At or near the maximum of this 24-period window, against a p75 of 107.2%, this is now the fastest reading in the series.

insights.title: Non-food credit hits ₹222.8L Cr — new record, up ₹3.2L Cr
insights.body: Non-food credit outstanding reached ₹222.8L Cr in August 2026, the highest level on record. Volume climbed ₹3.2L Cr period-on-period (₹219.6L Cr → ₹222.8L Cr), continuing the climb from ₹178.1L Cr in January 2025.
insights.implication: August's ₹3.2L Cr gain built on an already record-high base, leaving non-food credit at its highest level in this 36-period window.

inferences: Non-food credit outstanding rose to ₹222.8L Cr in August 2026, up ₹3.2L Cr from July's ₹219.6L Cr.
The book has grown from ₹178.1L Cr in January 2025 to ₹222.8L Cr now — an addition of roughly ₹44.6L Cr.
At or near the maximum of this 36-period window, the expansion shows no sign of a pause.

insights.title: Non-food credit added ₹29.2L Cr net new in FY26
insights.body: Banks deployed ₹29.2L Cr of net new non-food credit in the year ending March 2026. The figure is locked at ₹29.2L Cr across the window, reflecting the FY26 year-end tally fixed since March 2026.
insights.implication: ₹29.2L Cr is the largest annual non-food credit addition in this 36-period record, the high-water mark of the window.

inferences: Net new non-food credit in FY26 totalled ₹29.2L Cr.

It sits at or near the maximum of this window, the largest annual non-food credit addition in the dataset.

insights.title: Non-food credit growth eases to 18.8% YoY from 19.1%
insights.body: Non-food credit grew 18.77% year-on-year in August 2026. Growth slipped 0.29 points, from 19.06% to 18.77%.
insights.implication: This is the first pullback after a multi-month climb, but at 18.77% growth is still well above the 15.5% level that marks the top quarter of readings in this window.

inferences: Non-food credit grew 18.77% YoY in August 2026, down from 19.06% the prior period.
Even after this dip, 18.77% sits above the 15.5% upper bound of this signal's 24-period range.
The run-up that took growth from 9.3% in June 2025 to a peak near 19.1% has paused for the first time in this window.

insights.title: All 4 main sectors stay positive YoY, 36 periods running
insights.body: All four main credit sectors posted positive year-on-year growth in August 2026. Breadth held at 4 of 4 sectors, unchanged from the prior period.
insights.implication: Breadth has sat at its ceiling for 36 straight periods with no sector falling away, a sharp contrast to the 0-of-4 reading that held through August 2024.

inferences: 4 of 4 main sectors showed positive YoY growth in August 2026, matching every period since September 2024.
That streak now runs 36 periods, the maximum reading in this window, after a stretch of 0 of 4 through August 2024.
No sector has dropped out of positive growth since the count first turned to 4 of 4.

insights.title: Agriculture's credit share slips to 12.23%, near its lowest
insights.body: Agriculture's share of total bank credit fell to 12.23% in Aug 2026, down from 12.33% the previous period. The share declined 0.09 points to 12.23%, in the bottom quarter of readings across this 36-period window.
insights.implication: Agriculture's share of the book has been easing since early 2026, now back at the 12.2% level last touched in Nov 2023 — a sustained drift to the low end of this window rather than a one-period move.

inferences: Agriculture's share of total credit fell to 12.23% in Aug 2026, down 0.09 points from 12.33% in Jul 2026.
That reading sits in the bottom quarter of this 36-period window, matching the 12.2% level last seen in Nov 2023.
The share has stayed at or below 12.4% in every period since Jan 2026, after running near 12.7%-12.8% through most of 2024.

insights.title: Agriculture credit growth climbs to 17.22% YoY, a new high
insights.body: Agriculture credit grew 17.22% year-on-year in Aug 2026, up from 16.98% the previous period. Growth accelerated 0.25 points from 16.98% to 17.22%, its highest reading in this 24-period window.
insights.implication: Agriculture lending is now growing faster than at any point in this 24-period window, having more than doubled its pace since the 6.8% low of Jun 2025, with the climb resuming for four straight periods after April's brief dip.

inferences: Agriculture credit YoY growth rose to 17.22% in Aug 2026, up from 16.98% in Jul 2026 — a 0.25-point gain.
That is above the high end of this 24-period window's typical range, which topped out at 15.5%, making it the strongest reading shown.
Growth has risen from 6.8% in Jun 2025 to 17.22% now, climbing for four straight periods after dipping to 13.7% in Apr 2026.

insights.title: Industry credit: FY26 growth up 6.8 points over FY25
insights.body: Industry credit grew 8.2% in the year to Mar 2025 and 15.0% in the year to Mar 2026. Full-year growth stepped up 6.8 points between FY25 and FY26, set once at the Mar 2026 year-end rather than moving month to month.
insights.implication: Industry's full-year growth nearly doubled between FY25 and FY26 (8.2% to 15.0%), a 6.8-point step-up that stands as the reading recorded at the Mar 2026 close.

inferences: Industry credit grew 8.2% in FY25 and 15.0% in FY26 — a 6.8-point step-up in full-year growth.
This is an annual reading fixed at the Mar 2026 year-end; it holds steady between fiscal year-ends rather than moving month to month.
Industry's full-year pace nearly doubled between the two fiscal years, from 8.2% to 15.0%.

insights.title: Industry's credit share falls to 21.53%, back near its low
insights.body: Industry's share of total bank credit fell to 21.53% in Aug 2026, down from 21.86% the previous period. The share dropped 0.33 points to 21.53%, slipping into the bottom quarter of readings across this 36-period window.
insights.implication: Industry's share has slipped back to the 21.5% level last seen from Jan through Apr 2026, giving up the brief run-up to 21.9% seen in Jun and Jul.

inferences: Industry's share of total credit fell to 21.53% in Aug 2026, down 0.33 points from 21.86% in Jul 2026.
That puts it in the bottom quarter of this 36-period window, matching the 21.5% readings seen from Jan through Apr 2026.
The share had briefly run higher at 21.9% in Jun and Jul 2026 before this period's drop back to the 21.5% band.

insights.title: Industry credit growth eases to 18.23% YoY from its peak
insights.body: Industry credit grew 18.23% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down from 19.95% the previous period. Growth slowed 1.72 points from 19.95% to 18.23%, pulling back from Jul 2026's peak of 20.0% but still above the high end of this window's typical range, which topped out at 14.7%.
insights.implication: Industry credit growth pulled back from its window peak of 20.0% to 18.23% — the first easing after a run-up from 7.3% in Sep 2025 — but the reading still sits above the top of this window's typical range.

inferences: Industry credit YoY growth eased to 18.23% in Aug 2026, down 1.72 points from 19.95% in Jul 2026.
Jul 2026's 20.0% was the peak of this 24-period window; Aug 2026 is the first pullback from that peak.
Even after the pullback, 18.23% is still above the high end of this window's typical range, which topped out at 14.7%.

insights.title: Personal Loans is the biggest slice of the parent category at 32.7%
insights.body: Personal Loans holds the largest share of the parent category at 32.7%, Services 28.3%; Agriculture and Allied Activities is the smallest at 12.2%. These are size shares, not growth rates. Top three hold 82.5% of the parent category, spread 20.5 percentage points.
insights.implication: Composition, not momentum: Personal Loans carries the most weight of the parent category. Concentration means the big blocks drive the category — watch them first.

inferences: Personal Loans is the largest block at 32.7% of the parent category.
Agriculture and Allied Activities is the smallest at 12.2% — a 20.5 percentage points spread across 4 sub-categories.
The top three hold 82.5% of the parent category — concentrated mix.

insights.title: Services growing fastest at 24.3%; Personal Loans slowest at 16.9%
insights.body: Services leads YoY growth at 24.3%, Industry at 18.2%; Personal Loans is slowest at 16.9%. 4 of 4 categories growing, spread 7.4 percentage points.
insights.implication: Services is the fastest at 24.3% and the largest block at 28.1% of the category — pace and weight point the same way. Most of the category is growing.

inferences: Services is the standout at 24.3% YoY.
Personal Loans is the weakest at 16.9% — a spread of 7.4 percentage points across 4 categories.
4 of 4 categories are growing — broad-based momentum.

insights.title: Personal loans share steady at 32.71%, near its median
insights.body: Personal loans account for 32.71% of total bank credit in Aug 2026, unchanged from last period. Share held flat at 32.71%, remaining near the median of its 36-period range of 32.6% to 33.0%.
insights.implication: Personal loans' share is flat at 32.71% for a second straight period, sitting in the middle of its 32.6%–33.0% range rather than extending the prior period's move back toward the median.

inferences: Personal loans held 32.71% of total credit, unchanged from 32.71% last period.
The share sits near the median of its 36-period range (p25 32.6%, p75 33.0%).
With no movement this period, the segment is neither gaining nor losing ground in the mix.

insights.title: Personal loans growth hits fresh high of 16.92% YoY
insights.body: Personal loans credit grew 16.92% year-on-year in Aug 2026, the highest reading in this 24-period series. Growth accelerated from 16.23% to 16.92%, a 0.69-point gain, extending a climb that ran from 11.7% in Sep 2025 to 14.0% in Oct 2025 and now 16.92%.
insights.implication: Personal loans growth has broken its own record again, climbing 0.69 points to 16.92% — the fastest pace in this dataset, still accelerating rather than leveling off after last period's high.

inferences: Personal loans grew 16.92% YoY, up 0.69 points from 16.23% last period.
This is the strongest reading in the 24-period series, above the prior range of 11.9% to 15.3%.
The run continues from 11.7% in Sep 2025 through 14.0% in Oct 2025 to 16.92% now.

insights.title: Services credit stays at 7.0-point FY step-up: 12% to 19%
insights.body: Services credit grew 12.0% in FY25 and 19.0% in FY26, a 7.0-point acceleration. The full-year step-up, set at the Mar 2026 year-end, holds at 7.0pp, unchanged since last measured.
insights.implication: Services credit's move from 12.0% in FY25 to 19.0% in FY26 remains the sharpest full-year step-up in this dataset, a reading that stays fixed until the next March print.

inferences: Services credit grew 12.0% in FY25 and 19.0% in FY26.
That is a 7.0-point jump in the full-year growth rate between the two year-ends.
As an annual metric, this reading stays fixed until the next March year-end.

insights.title: Services share ticks up to 28.27%, above its typical range
insights.body: Services account for 28.27% of total bank credit in Aug 2026. Share rose 0.05pp from 28.22% to 28.27%, holding above the p75 mark of 27.9% in its 36-period range.
insights.implication: Services' share edged up to 28.27% after last period's flat reading, keeping the sector above the top quartile (27.9%) of its 36-period range rather than reverting toward the median.

inferences: Services held 28.27% share of total credit, up 0.05pp from 28.22% last period.
This sits above the p75 level of 27.9% across the 36-period range (p25 27.5%).
After holding flat last period, the share has ticked higher again.

insights.title: Services credit hits 24.35% YoY growth — highest in 24 periods
insights.body: Services credit grew 24.35% year-on-year in Aug 2026, the highest reading in this 24-period dataset. Growth accelerated from 22.94% to 24.35%, a 1.40-point gain, continuing a climb from 19.0% in Mar 2026 through 18.6%, 20.4%, 21.4%, 22.9%, to 24.3% now.
insights.implication: Services credit keeps re-accelerating rather than leveling off — at 24.35% it is the highest reading in the 24-period dataset, well above the typical 10.6%-to-18.0% range.

inferences: Services credit grew 24.35% YoY in Aug 2026, up from 22.94% the prior period — a 1.40-point gain.
That puts growth at the top of this 24-period window, whose typical range runs 10.6% to 18.0%.
The series shows growth climbing from a low of 8.4% in May 2025 to 24.35% now, roughly tripling over that stretch.

insights.title: Services took 35.0% of all new bank credit in the past year
insights.body: Of the bank credit added over the past twelve months, Services took 35.0% — the largest share of the new money — growing 24.3% a year and accelerating (+1.40 pp). The rest went to Personal Loans 30.0%; Industry 21.0%; Agriculture and Allied Activities 11.4%. Industry took 21.0% while growing 18.2% a year and slowing (-1.72 pp) — a smaller slice of a faster-growing total, not a retreat.
insights.implication: Shares of new lending move far faster than shares of the book, so this is the earlier read of the two. It says where the money went, not why — and a falling share alongside rising growth means the others grew faster, not that this one shrank.

inferences: Every sector's bank credit is compared with the same month a year earlier, and each one's share of the total increase is taken.
Services accounts for 35.0% of the increase.
All sectors moved the same way this window, so the shares of the net increase are bounded and sum to a hundred.

insights.title: Large is the biggest slice of the parent category at 66.5%

Medium is the smallest at 10.2% — a 56.4 percentage points spread across 3 sub-categories.
The top three hold 100.0% of the parent category — concentrated mix.

insights.title: Medium growing fastest at 31.8%; Large slowest at 14.9%

insights.implication: Medium is the fastest at 31.8% and the largest block at 2.2% of the category — pace and weight point the same way. Most of the category is growing.

inferences: Medium is the standout at 31.8% YoY.
Large is the weakest at 14.9% — a spread of 16.9 percentage points across 3 categories.
3 of 3 categories are growing — broad-based momentum.

insights.title: Large corporate share falls to 66.55% — new low in 36 periods
insights.body: Large corporates held 66.55% of industry credit in Aug 2026, down from 67.26% in the prior period. Share fell from 67.26% to 66.55%, breaking the plateau that had held it between 67.2% and 67.4% for several periods, and now sits at or near the lowest level in this 36-period window, below the 67.5% mark that most readings in this window sit above.
insights.implication: The 0.71-point drop to 66.55% ends the recent plateau between 67.2% and 67.4%, leaving large corporates at or near their lowest share of industry credit in this 36-period window.

inferences: Large corporate share fell to 66.55% in Aug 2026, down 0.71 points from 67.26% the prior period.
This breaks the plateau that had held the share between 67.2% and 67.4% for the preceding periods.
The reading sits at or near the minimum of this 36-period range, below the 67.5% level most readings in this window sit above.
Large corporates are losing share of industry credit at a pace the recent plateau had not shown.

insights.title: Large corporate credit growth cools to 14.9% from 17.7% peak
insights.body: Large corporate credit grew 14.88% YoY in Aug 2026, down from 17.69% in the prior period. Growth decelerated from 17.69% to 14.88%, a 2.81-point slowdown that breaks the run-up from 5.5% in Jan 2026. insights.implication: The 2.81-point deceleration to 14.88% is the first break in the run-up from 5.5% in Jan 2026 to 17.69% in Jul 2026, though growth remains well above the 8.8% level, among the strongest readings in this window.

inferences: Large corporate credit grew 14.88% YoY in Aug 2026, down 2.81 points from 17.69% the prior period.
This breaks the seven-period run-up that had taken growth from 5.5% in Jan 2026 to 17.69% in Jul 2026.
Even after the slowdown, 14.88% stays above the 8.8% level, keeping it among the strongest readings in this 24-period window.
The acceleration that had been building since January has broken step for the first time in this series.

insights.title: Medium enterprises share hits 10.19% — new high
insights.body: Medium enterprises held 10.19% of industry credit in Aug 2026, the highest share in this 36-period window. Share rose from 9.99% in Jul 2026 to 10.19% in Aug 2026, up 0.20pp, extending a run of new highs since 8.0% in Sep 2023.
insights.implication: Medium enterprises' share has climbed to 10.19%, clear of the historical p75 of 9.6% — the steadiest structural gain among the industry-size segments in this window.

inferences: Medium enterprises reached 10.19% of industry credit in Aug 2026, up 0.20pp from 9.99% in Jul 2026.
This sits at or near the maximum of the 36-period window, whose typical range runs from 8.5% to 9.6% (p25-p75).
The share has risen from 8.0% in Sep 2023 to 10.19% now, with no period of reversal in between.
Medium continues to hold a larger slice of industry credit than at any other point in this series.

insights.title: Medium enterprise credit growth hits 31.78% YoY, a fresh high
insights.body: Medium enterprise credit grew 31.78% YoY in Aug 2026, the fastest pace in this 24-period window. Growth accelerated from 30.48% in Jul 2026 to 31.78% in Aug 2026, up 1.30pp, the third straight month above 30%.
insights.implication: Medium enterprises have posted three consecutive months above 30% YoY growth, each one higher than the last — a sustained climb to a new ceiling for the segment rather than a single-period spike.

inferences: Medium enterprise credit grew 31.78% YoY in Aug 2026, up 1.30pp from 30.48% in Jul 2026.
This is the third consecutive period above 30%, following 30.3% in Jun 2026 and 30.5% in Jul 2026.
The typical range over this 24-period window is 17.1% to 21.1% (p25-p75), well below the current reading.
Growth is still rising each period rather than levelling off at its new highs.

insights.title: Micro & Small credit: 8.9% to 32.7% — 23.8pp FY step-up
insights.body: Micro & Small enterprise credit grew 8.9% in the year ending Mar 2025 and 32.7% in the year ending Mar 2026, a 23.8 percentage point acceleration. Full-year growth moved from 8.9% in FY25 to 32.7% in FY26 — a 23.8-point step-up, the largest in this dataset.
insights.implication: An acceleration of this size — taking the FY25 pace of 8.9% to 32.7% in FY26 — is the largest full-year step-up recorded for this segment in this dataset.

inferences: Micro & Small credit grew 8.9% in the year ending Mar 2025 and 32.7% in the year ending Mar 2026, an acceleration of 23.8pp.

FY26 marks a distinct, sustained step-up in the pace at which Micro & Small credit expanded across that full year.

insights.title: Micro & Small share rebounds to 23.26%, up 0.51pp
insights.body: Micro & Small enterprises held 23.26% of industry credit in Aug 2026, up 0.51pp from the prior period. Share rose from 22.75% in Jul 2026 to 23.26% in Aug 2026, reversing the near-flat readings of Jun 2026 (22.7%) and Jul 2026 (22.75%).
insights.implication: After two periods of near-flat share around 22.7-22.75%, Micro & Small's 0.51pp jump to 23.26% breaks that plateau, though the segment is still short of its Jan 2026 high of 23.5%.

inferences: Micro & Small share rose to 23.26% in Aug 2026, up 0.51pp from 22.75% in Jul 2026.

The reading now sits above the historical p75 of 22.7% for this 36-period window.

insights.title: Micro & Small growth reaccelerates to 22.96%, ending 4-period slide
insights.body: Micro & Small enterprise credit grew 22.96% YoY in Aug 2026, up 0.40pp from the prior period. Growth had decelerated for four straight periods from a Mar 2026 peak of 32.7% down to 22.56% in Jul 2026; it has now turned up to 22.96% in Aug 2026.
insights.implication: After four consecutive months of slowing from the Mar 2026 peak of 32.7%, Micro & Small's uptick to 22.96% in Aug 2026 is the first reversal in that slide, even as the pace stays far off the peak.

inferences: Micro & Small credit grew 22.96% YoY in Aug 2026, up 0.40pp from 22.56% in Jul 2026.

The segment's growth rate has stopped falling, though it remains well below its Mar 2026 peak of 32.7%.

insights.implication: The spread's rebound to 8.1pp breaks a six-period narrowing run that had brought MSME and large-corporate growth to within 4.9pp of each other, the closest gap since Mar 2025's 2.1pp.

inferences: The MSME-large corporate growth spread widened to 8.1pp in Aug 2026, up 3.2pp from 4.9pp in Jul 2026.

The 8.1pp reading sits near the median of this 24-period window.
MSME credit has pulled back ahead of large corporate credit after the gap had nearly closed.
